paper_title: SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into   One Separator
model_annotation:
This plot illustrates the training loss curves over iterations for several language model variants. The x-axis represents "#Iteration" on a linear scale, ranging from 0 to 140,000, with tick labels at intervals of 20,000. The y-axis represents "Loss" on a linear scale, ranging from approximately 2.4 to 3.4, with tick labels at intervals of 0.1.

Six lines are shown, each corresponding to a different model configuration. The purple line labeled "Vanilla" starts at approximately 3.4 at iteration 0 and decreases steeply in the early iterations, then gradually levels off, reaching approximately 2.50 by iteration 140,000. The blue line labeled "StrmLLM (n=64)" follows a similar initial steep decline from around 3.4 but converges to a notably higher loss value of approximately 2.62 at iteration 140,000, remaining consistently above most other lines throughout training. The orange line labeled "SepLLM (n=64)" starts near 3.4 and decreases to approximately 2.52 by iteration 140,000, closely tracking the Vanilla line. The green line labeled "SepLLM (n=64, H)" exhibits a very similar trajectory to the orange SepLLM (n=64) line, ending at approximately 2.52 at iteration 140,000. The red line labeled "SepLLM (n=64, H/T)" also follows a comparable path, ending at approximately 2.51 by iteration 140,000. The dark blue line labeled "SepLLM (n=128)" starts around 3.4 and decreases to approximately 2.60 at iteration 140,000, positioning it between the StrmLLM line and the cluster of SepLLM (n=64) variants. All lines show rapid loss reduction in the first approximately 20,000 iterations, after which the rate of decrease slows considerably. Each line appears to have a shaded region around it indicating variability or confidence bounds.
